title: A morning routine with a 6:15 AM hard stop
summary: Sixty minutes, five stations, one door. The hard stop is the whole design.

blocks.title: Out the door at 6:15, no matter what
blocks.body: The routine is not a list of aspirations. It is a conveyor with a hard stop at the end: whatever is not done by 6:15 does not go. Everything below fits inside that rule.

items.title: Up, lights on
items.detail: Alarm across the room. Standing up is the first task, and it is non-negotiable.

items.title: Coffee and water
items.detail: Kettle was loaded last night. No decisions before caffeine - that is the point of the prep.

items.title: Twenty minutes of movement
items.detail: Whatever is on the card. The card was written Sunday.

items.title: Shower and dress
items.detail: Clothes are out already. See 5:20: no decisions.

items.title: Bag, lunch, keys
items.detail: The launch pad by the door was stocked last night. This station is a check, not a search.

items.title: Hard stop
items.detail: Door. If something got skipped, tonight's prep fixes it - not tomorrow morning's panic.

blocks.title: Why the stop matters more than the routine
blocks.body: A morning routine without a hard stop is a wish list that shrinks under pressure. The stop is what makes the hour honest: it ends the same way on good days and bad ones, and it moves every failure to the evening, where there is time to fix it.
